💡 Key Takeaways
  • Celtic will encounter a European first when they take on Torreense in Portugal on Thursday night.
  • It will be the only time the Hoops have faced an opponent from the second tier of their domestic league in a Uefa competition as a result of Torreense claiming the first major trophy in the club's 109-year history last season.
  • Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic will encounter a European first when they take on Torreense in Portugal on Thursday night.

It will be the only time the Hoops have faced an opponent from the second tier of their domestic league in a Uefa competition as a result of Torreense claiming the first major trophy in the club's 109-year history last season.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Their shock 2-1 victory over Sporting Lisbon in the final of the Portuguese Cup in May to qualify for Europe for the first time in their history was the stuff of fairtytale. Think second tier Raith Rovers beating Celtic in the League Cup final in 1994.

Of course, by the time Raith came to play in the UEFA Cup the following season, they had gone on to earn promotion to the top flight. Not so Torreense. They lost 2-0 on aggregate to Casa Pia in the promotion/relegation play-off, meaning they remained in Liga Portugal 2 for the 2026/27 campaign.

They have since parted company with their cup-winning manager Luís Tralhão, who was sacked last month after overseeing a poor start to the domestic season, and replaced him with former Estrela da Amadora boss João Nuno.

Torreense currently occupy a lowly 13th spot in Liga Portugal 2 and will host Celtic in Leiria, 60 miles away from their home in Torres Vedras, as their own stadium only has 2,500 seats and does not meet Uefa requirements.

But park any thoughts of this fixture providing a banker win for Celtic. Torreense have already beaten Lillestrom and Ararat-Armenia in the Europa League and took the lead against Sunderland before the Premier League side netted a stoppage-time winner.

They sit 19th in the Europa League table, a lofty 13 places above Celtic, who belatedly put their first points on the board with a 3-2 win over Besiktas on November 5 after losing to Ferencváros, Benfica and Celta Vigo.

Nonetheless, this is a match Celtic should be looking to win if they are to retain realistic ambitions of becoming the first team to reach the knockout phase of the competition after losing their opening three league phase matches.

This is their most winnable tie on paper and failure to garner three points would leave Martin O'Neill's men with minimal margin for error in their remaining three fixtures - away to Omonoia, home to Marseille, then away to Union Saint-Gilloise.

Ten points, and a reasonably healthy goal difference is expected to be the benchmark for reaching the knockout play-off round. Nine points may be enough, but 11 points is the target to be absolutely sure.

Celtic should be looking at trips to Torreense and Omonoia, currently fifth in the Cypriot league, as an opportunity to reach nine points before facing the French and Belgian massive-hitters in their final two matches.

A familiar face awaits them at the Dr. Magalhães Pessoa Stadium. Former Hearts striker Musa Drammeh has been with the Portuguese club since departing Tynecastle in the summer of 2025.

He was part of their cup-winning squad last season and has played 17 times this term, scoring two goals.

The 24-year-old Spaniard has history with Celtic, having made his SPFL debut against them in a 2-0 defeat at Parkhead in September 2024, and then scoring his first Hearts goal in a 4-1 loss at Tynecastle two months later.

#198285. Transfer news: Major Saudi Pro League rule change could shake up the market

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (572 w)

Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Transfer news: Major Saudi Pro League rule change could shake up the market

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (572 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:26.
  • Sources indicate that with a little over a month to go until the transfer window reopens, clubs around the world are already moving behind the scenes to strengthen their squads.
  • According to The Times, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) is considering raising the limit on foreign players ahead of the 2027-28 window, which could trigger a fresh wave of signings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:26.

Sources indicate that with a little over a month to go until the transfer window reopens, clubs around the world are already moving behind the scenes to strengthen their squads. Saudi Arabia, which has become a leading player in the market in recent years, is considering a change that could boost its domestic league but worry other countries.

According to The Times, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) is considering raising the limit on foreign players ahead of the 2027-28 window, which could trigger a fresh wave of signings. Saudi clubs are seeking clarification on the matter before the Northern Hemisphere winter window in January.

Sources indicate that at present, clubs in Saudi Arabia can register up to eight foreign players in a 25-man squad, with the option of adding two more foreign under-21 players for SPL matches. The idea is to raise that limit to 14 or more, with discussions still ongoing.

According to recent reports, should the new rule come into force, Saudi clubs are likely to make more international signings. That could mark a new phase of departures from Europe to join the Saudi project, which aims to improve the competitive level of local football before the country hosts the World Cup in 2034.

In January 2023, Cristiano Ronaldo joined Al-Nassr after terminating his contract with Manchester United, which began a series of Saudi investments in football. In June of that year, the Public Investment Fund (PIF) took control of the four biggest domestic clubs: Al-Ahli, Al-Hilal, Al-Ittihad and Al-Nassr, the Portuguese star's team.

Then Ballon d'Or winner Karim Benzema was another high-profile name to leave Real Madrid for the Saudi Pro League, followed by stars such as N'Golo Kante and Roberto Firmino. Over the past three seasons, Neymar, Ollie Watkins, Gabriel Martinelli, Tijjani Reijnders, Darwin Nunez, Ivan Toney, Sadio Mane and Joao Felix have also been tempted by the Middle East.

As well as drawing global attention to its league, Saudi Arabia believes the move has helped the development of its homegrown talent. Competing for starting places with foreign stars encourages local players to improve.

On the other hand, critics of the proposal to raise the limit on non-Saudi players argue that the rule change could force local players to move abroad, or even leave bigger clubs for smaller ones, in order to get playing time.

It is worth remembering that the PIF has reduced its international sports investments, to the point of ending its backing of LIV Golf. In April, the fund revealed a five-year programme with a greater focus on domestic investment. Privatisations of Saudi clubs have also been recurring, such as the sale of 70 per cent of Al-Hilal in August.

Sources indicate that because of the geopolitical context in the region, including Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Yemen-based Houthi rebels, there is some uncertainty over the league's ability to attract foreign players in the short term. In October, the airport in the capital, Riyadh, was hit by a missile attack that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

In a recent development, the Asian Cup, which was due to be held in the country between January and February 2027, was postponed earlier this month. Three SPL matches were also postponed after the October Houthi attacks, although organisers did not attribute the decision to the conflict, saying it was motivated by 'logistical considerations'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that this article contains affiliate links. We may earn a small commission on items purchased through this article, but that does not affect our editorial judgement.

Hearts will attempt to claim a major European scalp when they host French giants Monaco in the Uefa Conference League on Thursday evening.

Wouter Vrancken’s side go into the match as underdogs but are in need of a positive result after collecting just one point from their opening three league phase fixtures to sit 32nd in the Conference League table.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A 1-1 draw against Norwegian side Nordsjælland at Tynecastle was followed by away defeats at Trabzonspor (2-0) and FC Thun (3-1) to leave the Tynecastle club facing an uphill task to qualify for the knockout stages.

Teams typically need seven or eight points from their six league phase matches to finish inside the top 24 and reach the knockout play-off round. Eight points virtually guarantees progression, while seven points usually puts a club right on the cut-off line where tie-breakers decide who advances.

Hearts know this only too well, having failed to progress on goals scored after collecting seven points to finish 25th during their 2024-25 Conference League campaign.

Industry observers note that monaco arrive in Edinburgh fourth in the table with a maximum haul of nine points following victories over CSKA Sofia, Nordsjælland and Freiburg. Their domestic form has been less impressive of late with Filipe Luís’ side at the moment on a five-game winless run on Ligue 1, where they are eighth in the standings.

The Conference League match between Hearts and Monaco takes place at Tynecastle Park, Edinburgh, on Thursday, November 26, 2026. Kick-off is 5.45pm.

The match will be shown live on TNT Sports 3 with coverage starting at 5pm.

Fans can stream the match live via HBO Max or Amazon Prime Video with a TNT Sports subscription.

Free highlights will be posted on the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel shortly after full-time.

It has been revealed that hearts welcome midfielder Blair Spittal back into their Europa League squad following his recovery from an ankle injury. Malachi Fagan-Walcott drops out with a groin problem. Two players who featured in the 8-0 win over Dundee on Saturday, Eduardo Ageu and Leart Kabashi, cannot play as they are not registered in the Europa League squad list.

It has been revealed that midfielder Tomas Magnusson is still completing concussion protocol before he can be declared available. Defender Craig Halkett and the versatile Oisin McEntee were back on the Riccarton training pitch on Wednesday, although they will not be back until next month. Winger Calvin Miller has also undergone surgery on his knee and will be out for between six weeks and two months.

Stephen Kingsley (hamstring), Harry Milne (knee) and Tom Renaud (ankle) are also unavailable.

According to recent reports, monaco are without five players. Goalkeeper Philippe Kohn, defender Mohammed Salisu, midfielders Stanis Idumbo and Aleksandr Golovin, plus forward Paris Brunner were all left in the Principality for treatment.

An all-German officiating team will take charge of the match. Daniel Schlager is the on-field referee and will be supported on the touchlines by assistant referees Sven Waschitzki and Tobias Fritsch. Robin Braun has been appointed as the fourth official. In the video operations room, Benjamin Cortus will serve as the Video Assistant Referee (VAR), alongside Nicolas Winter as the Assistant VAR (AVAR).

Hearts 11/2, Draw 18/5, Monaco 8/15 - via oddschecker.com.

#198277. The brain keeps the score: how trauma leaves molecular scars in cells

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (790 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

The brain keeps the score: how trauma leaves molecular scars in cells

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (790 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library.
  • A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering new insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.
  • Industry observers note that the study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers examined DNA methylation in brain regions, including the amygdala and hippocampus, which are parts of the limbic system shown here.Credit: K H Fung/Science Photo Library.

A post-mortem analysis of more than 300 people is offering new insights into how trauma chemically alters the brain.

Industry observers note that the study, published in Cell Reports on 20 November1, identifies molecular changes to DNA inside the brain cells of people with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and depression. These include ‘epigenetic marks’ — chemical tags added to DNA as a result of environmental influences, including stress and trauma. Epigenetic marks can affect how genes work, but do not alter DNA sequences.

The analysis “gives the most comprehensive look at cell type differences” in brain regions following PTSD diagnosis, states Alicia Smith, who studies the epigenetics of PTSD at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia.

It has been revealed that PTSD can develop after experiencing a traumatic event, causing symptoms such as flashbacks, anxiety and emotional distress. Understanding its epigenetic consequences helps researchers to track how trauma can alter gene regulation, and perhaps explain why some people experience symptoms and respond to treatment differently.

In a recent development, the study analysed postmortem brain tissues and medical records donated by 101 people who were diagnosed with PTSD, 101 people with depression and 100 control participants who did not have a mental-health condition. The researchers examined DNA methylation in brain cells — an epigenetic mechanism in which methyl groups are added to or removed from DNA sequences.

Sources indicate that many previous studies of epigenetic marks linked to PTSD have used samples of DNA from blood2 or saliva3. “What we really want to understand is what’s going on in the brain,” says study co-author Frances Champagne, a behavioural epigeneticist at the University of Texas at Austin.

Champagne and her colleagues examined DNA methylation across more than 850,000 genomic regions in cells taken from three parts of the brain: the amygdala, hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, which are involved in emotion processing, memory and cognitive control, respectively.

Sources indicate that the study found distinct methylation patterns in four DNA regions in the prefrontal cortex when comparing the PTSD group with the control group, but none in the amygdala or the hippocampus. One gene affected by these unique DNA methylations had not been previously linked to PTSD, but has a key role in memory.

In a recent development, the researchers also identified differences at the cellular level. Compared with the control group, the amygdala in people with PTSD had significantly reduced levels of oligodendrocytes — cells that create a protective, insulating sheath around the connections between neurons and facilitate communication between them.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’.

Recent findings suggest that the amygdala is central to fear responses. “That decrease in oligodendrocytes that we see in PTSD seems to be linked to, particularly, exposure to adult trauma,” notes Champagne. Oligodendrocytes were reduced across all three brain regions in 58 people who had experienced trauma as adults, regardless of whether or not they were diagnosed with a disorder. The researchers did not observe the same pattern in 97 donors who experienced childhood trauma.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:29.
  • Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has refused to confirm whether David Raya will be available for their Premier League showdown with Manchester City on Sunday afternoon.
  • The Spaniard missed Tuesday night's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League after picking up a shoulder injury against Newcastle United at the weekend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:29.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has refused to confirm whether David Raya will be available for their Premier League showdown with Manchester City on Sunday afternoon.

The Spaniard missed Tuesday night's 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League after picking up a shoulder injury against Newcastle United at the weekend.

Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised at the Emirates Stadium, with Arteta offering his backing to the goalkeeper should Raya remain unavailable this weekend.

Raya left the pitch in significant pain during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with the Magpies on Saturday night, prompting fears that he could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

However, subsequent scans proved positive, with the Spanish goalkeeper avoiding a serious injury and not requiring surgery.

There have been suggestions that Raya could only be sidelined for a matter of days and might therefore be in contention to face City, but Arteta was unwilling to offer any guarantees after the Dortmund draw.

"No, we have nothing to add today unfortunately," the Arsenal manager said (via the Evening Standard). "We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not [to face Man City].".

Arsenal will therefore have to wait for further clarity on their first-choice goalkeeper, with Kepa potentially required to retain his place against Enzo Maresca's side, who also drew at home to Napoli this midweek.

Kepa produced a reasonably solid display in Germany, with Arteta describing his performance as "really good" and insisting that Arsenal fully trust their goalkeepers.

The Spaniard made three saves and received a 7.5 Sofascore rating, making him the Gunners' third-best performer on the night. His expected goals prevented figure of 0.38 also reflected a positive contribution.

Sources indicate that there were, however, a few moments that offered cause for concern. Kepa was wrong-footed for Dortmund's goal, while he parried a disallowed effort back into a dangerous area and did not look as assured as Raya when dealing with crosses.

Arteta is nevertheless confident in his deputy, saying: "We fully trust our keepers and if he needs to play against City, he will play.".

Industry observers note that it is encouraging that Kepa has Arteta's backing, but there would understandably be some apprehension about him starting against a side of City's calibre. Raya's command of his penalty area and reliability have made him an notable figure for Arsenal, and his absence would be a significant setback.

However, if the first-choice goalkeeper is not ready, Kepa will have to step up when called upon.

They should be lifted for the league campaign by Tuesday night’s 6-1 Velocity Trophy win at Crowborough, with Jack Strange, Yoan Edoukou, George Vorster (2) and Shamir Fenelon (2) scoring.

Mansell was asked after the Stanway draw how he felt and noted: “The same as after the last few games with this little run that we’re in.

Recent findings suggest that "When we go 2-1 up we stop doing what we were doing. People think the right thing to do is to drop deep and tighten up. But all you do is invite pressure into areas where you then give away a cheap free-kick and you get punished.

In a recent development, "We need to be mentally stronger and control a game better by staying brave in possession and keeping the ball, which doesn’t allow them to have the ball. It’s all about playing the game in their half rather than our half.”.

Mansell does not think Hill were a long way off becoming a winning team again.

It has been revealed that "We’re struggling to get over the line because of nervousness around the group. This is a situation we haven’t been in for the three years I’ve been at the club,” he added.

Recent findings suggest that "All the games have been tight other than the Enfield game. I don’t think we’re a million miles away. We’re drawing games that could go either way. We just need to get one over the line to kick-start something.”.

According to recent reports, mansell thanked fans for continuing to turn up in good numbers. “It was a good turnout (at Stanway) considering how far we were from home. We do appreciate the support away from home.

"Stick with us, we’ll turn it round and get some wins and we will be smiling again.”.

They host in-form Eastbourne Borough on Saturday.

Sources indicate that mansell said: “We’re not going to shy away from anything. We’ll keep plugging away trying to win games. We’ll go into Saturday as positive as we can.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that this article contains affiliate links. We may earn a small commission on items purchased through this article, but that does not affect our editorial judgement.

Celtic are in Europa League action on Thursday night when they travel to Portugal to face second-tier side Torreense.

The game will mark the first time in history that the Hoops have contested a European fixture against a team who are not competing in the top flight of their domestic league.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Torreense qualified for the Europa League after a fairytale cup success last season, defying the odds to beat Sporting Lisbon in the final of the Portuguese Cup to claim the first major trophy in their 109-year existence.

They failed to secure promotion, however, losing 2-0 on aggregate to Casa Pia in the promotion/relegation play-off, meaning they remained in Liga Portugal 2 for the 2026/27 campaign, where they current sit 13th in the table.

Celtic put their first Europa League points on the board at the fourth attempt with a 3-2 win over Besiktas on November 5 following three consecutive defeats by Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo.

Martin O’Neill’s side sit 32nd in the 36-team league with four games to play as they bid to climb into the top 24 and become the first side to qualify for the knockout stages after losing their opening three league phase matches.

Torreense are in a healthier 19th position having collected six points from their opening four games with victories over Lillestrom and Ararat-Armenia mixed with defeats to Sunderland and Ferencvaros.

Recent findings suggest that the Europa League match between Torreense and Celtic will take place on Thursday, November 26, 2026 at the Dr. Magalhães Pessoa Stadium in Leiria. The venue is 60 miles away from Torreense’s actual home in Torres Vedras, as their own stadium only has 2,500 seats and does not meet Uefa requirements. Kick-off is 8pm.

The match will be shown live on TNT Sports 3 with coverage starting at 7.45pm, following on from Hearts v Monaco on the same channel.

Fans can stream the match live via HBO Max or Amazon Prime Video with a TNT Sports subscription.

Free highlights will be posted on the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel shortly after full-time.

Celtic have added Jota to their Europa League squad in place of the injured Mika Baur. The Portuguese winger was initially left out as he fought his way back from a serious knee injury. But he could now feature in his homeland against Torreense after continuing his comeback with a start in Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren. Baur was recently ruled out for up to 10 weeks with ankle ligament damage.

Benjamin Nygren is nursing a heel problem while Alistair Johnston remains sidelined by a hamstring injury.

Torreense are missing suspended Jorge Aguirre following his red card in the 3-2 win over Aararat-Armenia and the injured Adama Baradji.

Recent findings suggest that an all-Dutch officiating team will take charge of the match. Allard Lindhout is the on-field referee and he will be joined on the pitch by assistant referees Johan Balder and Murat Kucukerbir, while Jannick van der Laan serves as the fourth official. Pol van Boekel has been assigned as the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) with Dennis Johan Higler acting as the Assistant Video Assistant Referee (AVAR).

Torreense 4/1, Draw 7/2, Celtic 4/6 - via oddschecker.com.

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:34.

According to recent reports, paris Saint-Germain are still coming to terms with the loss of Desire Doue for at least six months because of a serious knee injury, and are making their final preparations to face Roma in the Champions League. One of Luis Enrique's biggest concerns ahead of the game is the red-hot form of Donyell Malen, Roma's top scorer.

In a recent development, at a press conference on Tuesday (24 November), the Spanish manager went out of his way to praise the Dutch forward, who already has 16 goals and four assists in 15 games for Roma this season. Luis Enrique highlighted Malen's improvement since January, when he moved to Italy and developed enormously under Gian Piero Gasperini, forcing Paris Saint-Germain to draw up a special containment blueprint.

'I am impressed with Donyell Malen and the number of goals he has scored, he has been great this season. Since he started playing as a centre-forward, he has been doing very well. We have to be very careful' - the manager remarked.

Paris Saint-Germain face Roma on Wednesday (25 November) at 8pm UK time at the Parc des Princes, on matchday five of the league phase. The Spanish boss will try to extend his side's perfect record to stay top of the table, while the Italian manager knows the importance of a surprise result to move towards the knockout phase, as Roma sit 20th with four points.

In a recent development, more than his goalscoring record, the number 14 concerns Luis Enrique because his profile enhances Gasperini's style of play: attacking runs in behind, control of the penalty area and a great ability to finish. Before Malen, Roma suffered from the lack of a player with those characteristics, as neither Artem Dovbyk nor Evan Ferguson had success in the first half of 2025-26.

The solution found by the manager was to use the winter transfer window to take the 27-year-old from Aston Villa, where he had few opportunities as a starter. In England, the Dutchman was used mostly as a winger by Unai Emery, but the Roma boss saw his potential to play in a more central role.

The six-month loan was the turning point for Roma, who climbed from sixth to third in Serie A, securing a return to the Champions League after an eight-year absence. With 14 goals and two assists in 18 league games, Malen was signed permanently from Aston Villa for £23m (€27m).

In 2026-27, thanks to the number 14's fluid partnership with Matias Soule, Paulo Dybala, Wesley, Rodrigo Mora and tech giant, Roma are established in the top four and are Serie A title contenders, sitting second with 30 points, two behind leaders Lazio after 12 matches. Roma have not been Italian champions since 2000-01.

Mobility is one of the Dutch forward's trademarks, as he often drops close to team-mates to offer a passing option during build-up and to create space in the opposition defence for others to advance. Out of possession, Malen is also a key part of Roma's pressing to win the ball back in favourable conditions for a shot.

In the best year of his career, the Roma number 14 is the biggest threat to Paris Saint-Germain's defensive system, which knows it cannot afford to slip. Otherwise, Malen is likely to punish the French side with his technical ability and finishing efficiency, even when chances are rare.

After Saturday’s win, Hinshelwood said the display showed his squad were learning as they went.

Industry observers note that he said: “It was probably one of our best wins if you look at where Harrogate are in the league and that we’d come off the back of that late goal conceded at Scunthorpe the previous week. We wanted a response to that and got it.

“They probably shaded the first half but we scored at a good time – in fact Jordan scored twice at good times.

According to recent reports, “At 1-1 we had a real go and shows how far we have come. Settling for a draw just isn’t in our mindset. We’ve had a few games that could have gone either way but we will always try to win games.

“The second goal came from the type of move we’ve been working on in training.”.

“He’s a top talent who we’d chased for a while. He’d done it against us too many times and we knew what he could do for us.”.

Young has scored six goals in 15 appearances and Hinshelwood remarked: “He is scoring, assisting and creating.”.

But Tuesday’s loss at Woking – where goals by Ashley Nathaniel-George and Dominic Johnson-Fisher (2) proved in vain – left Hinshelwood hugely frustrated.

According to recent reports, “We’re gifting games to our opponents. They don’t have to do anything to beat us. We scored two unbelievable goals but gifted them goals – and it’s a common trend,” he told club media.

It has been revealed that “Good teams are consistent week after week but we have turned up and just thought we can do enough to win. At this level you get found out.

Brighton striker Promise David is “in contention” to feature against Craiova as he looks to kick-start his Albion career following a difficult start to life on the south coast.

The Canadian international joined the Seagulls on a season-long loan from Belgian champions Union Saint-Gilloise in August.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The deal is believed to have an option to buy for around £20m but has so far Promise has struggled to make an impression in Fabian Hurzeler's first team.

David has totalled just 23 minutes of Premier League football without scoring and didn’t make the squad for the defeat at Hull.

In the Conference League the 25-year-old featured against Kauno Zalgiris and Jablonec but was not in the squad for the win at Getafe.

However, Hurzeler has indicated that the striker remains firmly in his thoughts ahead of the meeting against the Romanian league leaders at the Amex Stadium.

"He's a contender, like all the other players," said the Brighton head coach to Sussex World.

The Brighton boss also stressed that David must continue adapting to the physical demands of his methods, particularly the intensity required during training.

"It's getting step by step closer to the demands and the things we ask of him, especially regarding intensity," he explained.

Hurzeler compared David's situation to that of latest arrival Femi Azeez, insisting that players outside the starting XI must take responsibility for forcing their way into contention.

"Tobi [Promise] has to use every training session, no matter how long we're on the pitch, to be at his highest level. He needs to do extra work in the gym and extra work after training.

"If you're a non-starter, that's what I demand from the players. You shouldn't be happy with the situation. No player should be happy about being a non-starter and not playing in games.".

Promise arrived at Brighton with an impressive goalscoring record. He scored 41 goals in 82 appearances for Union Saint-Gilloise, helping the Belgian club to their first league title in 90 years.

He also has four goals in 18 appearances for Canada, including a goal at the 2026 World Cup.

Hurzeler believes the responsibility ultimately rests with the player to make the most of his opportunities.

"You need to take ownership and work as hard as possible because that's the only thing you can control," he remarked to Sussex World.

"You can complain about the situation, but I've learned one thing in life: complaining never helps. It's about doing the hard work and taking ownership of your own journey and your own process.".

'The main problem' - Enzo Maresca defends surprise Man City tactical decision after 2-2 Napoli draw

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (460 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:48.
  • Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has explained some of his unexpected selection and tactical decisions after his side were held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday evening.
  • The result saw City twice come from behind, but their defensive problems continued as they dropped further points in the Champions League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 07:48.

Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has explained some of his unexpected selection and tactical decisions after his side were held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday evening.

The result saw City twice come from behind, but their defensive problems continued as they dropped further points in the Champions League.

Maresca also acknowledged that his side are still searching for the right balance between attacking and defending following his arrival as Pep Guardiola's successor.

Maresca left Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye on the bench for the opening hour, while Phil Foden was also rested, prompting questions about his selection.

The City boss explained that his decisions were based on how he expected Napoli to set up, with the visitors having recently used a 3-5-2 or 3-5-1-1 formation.

"We expected Napoli to play 3-5-2 or 3-5-1-1 as they did in recent matches, so that would basically leave eight players in the middle, and hope to create more spaces down the wings," Maresca told Sky Sport Italia.

He wanted Rayan Cherki to operate out wide and exploit those spaces, although City struggled to turn their possession into enough chances during the first half.

Maresca also defended his decision to use Ayyoub Bouaddi in a deeper midfield role alongside Elliott Anderson, explaining that he wanted to maintain balance while allowing six players to attack.

However, the manager admitted that City's defensive shortcomings remain a significant concern.

"The main problem is that we are conceding too many goals, and we need to do something about that," he added.

Maresca also acknowledged that finding the right approach would take time, comparing City's transition to the challenges Arsenal and Manchester United experienced following the departures of Arsene Wenger and Sir Alex Ferguson.

It is not unusual for Maresca to rotate his City side during midweek fixtures, but leaving Doku, Ndiaye and Foden out of the starting lineup for a potentially important Champions League match was still a notable decision.

City ultimately rescued a point, but the draw could prove costly in their hopes of progressing in the competition, particularly given their recent struggles for consistency.

Perhaps Maresca also had this weekend's showdown with Premier League title rivals Arsenal in mind, with City travelling to the Emirates for Sunday's late kick-off.

That is not to suggest the manager deliberately sacrificed the Napoli fixture, but resting Foden and keeping two dangerous wide players in reserve could indicate that he was considering the demands of a huge domestic encounter.

City need to find greater defensive stability regardless of the opposition, as Maresca himself acknowledged, but Sunday's meeting with the Gunners may have been a factor in how he approached his midweek selection.
